canonical_statement: The study objective was to compare cardiovascular and renal effectiveness and safety of empagliflozin versus dapagliflozin using nationwide routine-practice data from Sweden, Denmark, and Norway.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The objective of this study was to compare the cardiovascular and renal effectiveness and safety of empagliflozin vs. dapagliflozin using nationwide data from routine clinical practice in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway.

canonical_statement: The investigators used an active-comparator new-user cohort design with individual-level nationwide register data from Sweden, Denmark, and Norway.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conducted a cohort study with an active-comparator new-user design, using individual-level data from national registers in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway.

canonical_statement: The study linked population, socioeconomic, patient, prescribed-drug, Swedish National Diabetes Register, and Danish laboratory-register data sources.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used data from population registers ... patient registers ... prescribed drug registers ... the Swedish National Diabetes Register ... and the Danish Register of Laboratory Results for Research.

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were 35–84 years old and were new users of empagliflozin or dapagliflozin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included patients, aged 35–84 years, who were new users of empagliflozin or dapagliflozin.

population.label: Eligible new users
inclusion_criteria: New use of empagliflozin or dapagliflozin

canonical_statement: Enrollment ran from 1 June 2014 to 30 June 2021 in Sweden and Denmark and from 1 June 2014 to 31 December 2018 in Norway.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: between 1 June 2014 and 30 June 2021 in Sweden and Denmark and between 1 June 2014 and 31 December 2018 in Norway.

population.label: Eligible new users

canonical_statement: New use was defined as no prior use of any SGLT2 inhibitor before cohort entry.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: New use was defined as no use of a SGLT2 inhibitor at any time before cohort entry.

population.label: Eligible new users
inclusion_criteria: No prior SGLT2 inhibitor use before cohort entry

canonical_statement: Patients without a recent glucose-lowering drug who also had prior chronic heart failure or chronic kidney disease were excluded to reduce inclusion of people receiving SGLT2 inhibitors for non-diabetes indications.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We excluded patients who did not use any glucose-lowering drug within 6 months before cohort entry and who also had a history of chronic heart failure or chronic kidney disease.

population.label: Eligible new users
exclusion_criteria: No glucose-lowering drug within 6 months plus prior chronic heart failure or chronic kidney disease

canonical_statement: Other exclusions included prior dialysis or renal transplantation, end-stage illness, drug misuse, severe pancreatic disorders, no specialist-care contact or prescription-drug use in the previous year, and any hospital admission within 30 days before cohort entry.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Further exclusion criteria were history of dialysis or renal transplantation, end stage illness, drug misuse, severe pancreatic disorders, neither use of any prescription drug nor any specialist care contact in the previous year, and hospital admission for any reason within 30 days before cohort entry.

population.label: Eligible new users
exclusion_criteria: No specialist care or prescription drug in prior year

canonical_statement: Empagliflozin was the study exposure; its recommended starting dose during the study period was 10 mg.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The recommended starting dose for both empagliflozin and dapagliflozin was 10 mg during the study period.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The recommended starting dose for both empagliflozin and dapagliflozin was 10 mg during the study period.

exposures.details: Recommended starting dose during the study period; active comparator.

canonical_statement: Major cardiovascular events were defined as a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Major cardiovascular events were defined as a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death.

outcome.definition: Composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Heart failure was defined as hospital admission for heart failure or death due to heart failure.

outcome.definition: Hospital admission for heart failure or death due to heart failure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Serious renal events were defined as a composite of renal replacement therapy, death from renal causes, and hospitalization for renal events.

outcome.definition: Composite of renal replacement therapy, death from renal causes, and hospitalization for renal events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Stroke was a secondary outcome.

canonical_statement: Any-cause death was a secondary outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Any-cause death was a secondary outcome.

canonical_statement: Diabetic ketoacidosis was analyzed as a serious adverse event outcome of concern.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Diabetic ketoacidosis was analyzed as a serious adverse event outcome of concern.

canonical_statement: Patients were followed from cohort entry until the outcome event, death, emigration, 5 years of follow-up, or the end of the study period, whichever occurred first.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were followed from cohort entry ... until outcome event, death, emigration, 5 years of follow-up, or end of study period.

canonical_statement: The main exposure definition treated patients as exposed to their cohort-entry drug throughout follow-up, analogous to an intention-to-treat design.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were defined as exposed to the study drug from cohort entry throughout follow-up, analogous to an intention-to-treat design in a clinical trial.

canonical_statement: Confounding adjustment used stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting based on a logistic propensity score containing 68 baseline covariates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used inverse probability of treatment weighting with stabilized weights to adjust for confounding. A logistic regression model was used to estimate the propensity score ... conditional on 68 baseline covariates.

canonical_statement: Propensity scores were estimated separately within each country, patients outside overlapping propensity-score regions were excluded, and analyses then used pooled data from the three countries.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The propensity scores were estimated in each country separately and patients outside the overlapping regions of the propensity score distribution were excluded. Analyses were performed on a pooled dataset from the three countries.

canonical_statement: Covariate balance after weighting was assessed with standardized differences, with absolute differences below 10% considered indicative of good balance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The covariate balance after weighting was assessed with standardized differences; differences of less than 10% were considered indicative of good balance.

canonical_statement: Adjusted hazard ratios were estimated with Cox proportional-hazards regression using time since treatment start as the time scale.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A Cox proportional hazards regression model with time since start of treatment as the time scale was used to estimate hazard ratios.

canonical_statement: Absolute rate differences were estimated with a Poisson model using an identity link.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The absolute rate difference was calculated using a Poisson model with identity link.

canonical_statement: Adjusted Kaplan–Meier estimates were used to describe cumulative incidence, with coprimary-outcome risk differences estimated at 1, 3, and 5 years and bootstrap confidence intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Risk differences for the coprimary outcomes at 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years after cohort entry were estimated by the adjusted Kaplan-Meier estimator, with 95% CIs estimated using bootstrapping.

canonical_statement: Prespecified subgroup analyses examined age, sex, history of major cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease; separate propensity scores were estimated within each subgroup and interaction P values below 0.05 were considered significant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conducted prespecified subgroup analyses ... A separate propensity score was estimated within each subgroup. Effect modification ... P-values of <0.05 were considered statistically significant.

canonical_statement: Prespecified laboratory-enhanced sensitivity analyses added HbA1c, blood pressure, albuminuria, eGFR, BMI, and smoking in Sweden and HbA1c, albuminuria, and eGFR in Denmark.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we expanded the propensity score to include additional variables ... glycated haemoglobin level, blood pressure, albuminuria, eGFR, body mass index, and smoking in Sweden and glycated haemoglobin level, albuminuria, and eGFR in Denmark.

canonical_statement: Missing additional laboratory/clinical variables in the sensitivity analyses were handled with fully conditional specification multiple imputation using 10 imputed datasets.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: multiple imputation (fully conditional specification imputation) with 10 imputed datasets was used.

canonical_statement: A prespecified as-treated sensitivity analysis considered patients exposed while prescriptions were refilled within the estimated duration of the most recent prescription plus a 30-day grace period.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were considered exposed and remaining on treatment as long as prescriptions were refilled within the estimated duration of the most recent prescription. A 30-day grace period was used.
